newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Cotton prices steady in Pakistan, up in India.
newsitem.headline: Cotton prices steady in Pakistan, up in India.

text.p: Cotton prices were steady in Pakistan amid low demand but firmed in India on fresh mill buying, dealers in the two countries said on Thursday.
Dealers in Karachi said prices gained slightly earlier in the week to Thursday but then remained steady amid low demand.
Most spinners were well-stocked while high domestic prices kept exporters out of the market.
The Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association (PCGA) said production from the 1996/97 (July-June) crop reached 8.335 million 375-lb bales by February 15 compared with 9.481 million in the year-ago period.

It said ginners had sold 6.531 million bales to textile mills compared with 6.994 million in the year-ago period and 5,400 bales to exporters compared with 1.128 million last year. Some 1.798 million bales remained unsold at ginneries.
A PCGA official said total production was likely to reach 8.7 million bales, compared with a target of 10 million and a 1995/96 crop of 9.94 million.
Dealers said rates remained steady despite small-scale buying by Japanese and Indonesian importers.
A Japanese buyer bought 1,000 bales at 69.20 U.S. cents per pound FOB on Monday and Indonesia 600 bales at 73.50 U.S. cents per pound C&F on Sunday, broker Nasim Usman said.

A member of the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said cotton export registrations, including these two deals, had reached 23,103 bales by Monday last, compared with 2.084 million bales by the same date last year.
Usman attributed the sharp fall in exports to high domestic prices. "Exports could pick up if prices fall to 2,000 rupees per maund (37.32 kg)," he said.
In the kerb market on Thursday, the NIAB-78 variety was quoted at 2,075 rupees per maund and MNH-93 at 2,375.
Following are the weekly cotton spot rates in rupees per maund issued by the private Karachi Cotton Association:
Thursday Wednesday Feb 13
In India prices recovered on fresh buying from mills and reduced new crop supplies in the northern region in the week to Thursday, traders there said.
"Lower prices have led farmers to cut down on supplies," said a trader.
Spot Bengal deshi rose 25/35 rupees to 785/825 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) and Punjab saw-ginned by 20/35 rupees to 1,410/1,630.
F-414 gained 40/60 rupees to 1,850/1,870 during the week. Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) rose 300/400 rupees to 11,400/11,600 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
Traders said average daily arrivals in the Punjab region fell during the week to 15,000/20,000 bales (170 kg each) from 20,000/30,000 in the previous week.
"Prices also rallied during the week on hopes that the government may authorise more cotton exports," said another trader.

The government has so far approved the export of 1.20 million bales of cotton. But Indian exporters have registered deals for only 450,000/500,000 bales and shipped barely 100,000/110,000, trader said.
They added that the Cotton Advisory Board (CAB) in the federal ministry of textiles would meet on Monday to assess the 1996/97 crop (Oct/Sept).
The CAB had at its last meeting estimated the crop at 15.50 million bales against 16 million in 1995/96.
